note: x/y/w/h are pixels within the sheet, checked against a render. Water: stream_* tiles for 1-wide streams, pond for a 3x3 pond. footprint = the tiles an entity occupies for collision and pushing, in tiles, anchored at the sprite's bottom-left tile; optional x is a column offset from that tile (default 0). Sprites without one occupy 1x1. Tall trees/rocks block only their bottom row so the player can walk behind the canopy. offset {x,y} is an optional pixel nudge applied when drawing. layer: ground (flat, under everything), object (y-sorted with the player), above (drawn over objects), overlay (whole screen); terrain tiles have no layer. anims: named frame ranges {from,to,fps?,loop?} in a strip; the player instead uses rows (dirs are columns) and poses [col,row]. pieces: true means each frame is a separate particle piece, pick one, do not animate. materials: what it is made of, main material first; mixed things list several. variants: related sprites by name, the same map on every member; becomes: what this turns into after an event. Added fields: kind ("sprite" default when absent, "sound", "music", "font"); loop and durationMs for audio; slice {l,t,r,b} = 9-slice border insets in pixels; grid {cellW,cellH,cols,chars} = bitmap-font glyph layout, chars[i] is the glyph in cell i read left-to-right, top-to-bottom (\u007f marks an empty cell); faceset = id of the actor's 38x38 dialog portrait. Actors whose animations live in separate files (bosses, SeparateAnim strips, ninja32) are one entry per file, linked by a shared variants map. Tags 'region' and 'kit' mark multi-tile autotile blocks or construction kits catalogued as one rectangle; the desc explains the layout. Grid sheets without rows/dirs anims (e.g. ninja32_jump, logic_*) number frames left-to-right, top-to-bottom.
